features: THE CREDIT YOU COULDN'T SPEND — The system has long been able to say how much credit an owner has. It has never been able to say which instalment that credit covers, and without that sentence the administrator, once on the payment screen, faces a list of instalments and has to work it out alone: the credit just sits there. While closing that loop, three places came to light where the product was hiding that credit or describing it wrongly. No migration, and no data changes on its own.

NOW IT SAYS WHAT IT COVERS. The «Credits to offset» dashboard widget no longer shows only the amount, but also the instalment that credit covers and its due date, and the link opens «New payment» already pointed at that instalment, not just at the person. The same sentence appears in the «Available credit» card of the account statement, next to a «Offset» link, and in the message that follows instalment issuing. When there is nothing to cover, it says so: a credit sitting idle is information, not silence — and certainly not an invitation to click through to a page where there is nothing to do.

TWO STATED LIMITS, so the advice is always actionable. The suggestion only considers issued instalments: proposing to offset a draft instalment would mean proposing a debt that does not yet exist for the owner. And it does not cross between ordinary and extraordinary management on its own: the system allows that and records it in the journal, but it asks the administrator for an explicit tick, and an automatic suggestion cannot take that as given. Credit on the other management is still counted in the total — it simply does not enter the proposal.

THE CREDIT THE OWNER SAW AND NO LONGER HAD. In the owner portal, the «Piggy bank» showed credit that had already been spent: the figure summed the original credit and ignored how much of it had already been consumed, so someone with a 300 € advance who had used 200 still saw 300, and the «Yes, settle the instalment with my credit» button computed on that figure. The only thing stopping the request was the server check, when the administrator opened the task. The figure is now computed at the moment the owner opens their instalment, instead of being written once when the plan is approved. That matters beyond the reported case: the old value stayed frozen even when shares changed, when an issue was cancelled, or when a payment was reversed.

THE BUTTON THAT WASN'T THERE, AND THE NOTICE THAT SENT YOU LOOKING FOR IT. When an owner asks from the portal to settle using their credit, the payment screen shows the administrator a notice. That notice behaved backwards: it disappeared when the credit was there — exactly when there was something to confirm — and stayed up when there was no credit, telling you to click a button that in that case is not on screen. The request now stays visible throughout, and the text says which of the two cases applies.

THE CREDIT HIDDEN IN INSTALMENTS THAT NET TO ZERO. If on the same instalment an owner has one overpaid share and one unpaid share that cancel out, the row comes to zero and the payment screen answered «N/D»: no field, no button. That credit exists, though, and can be spent on other instalments — the system has never required credit and debt to be on the same instalment. From this version the «Use credit» button appears where the credit really is, not where the row balance is negative. The row is still marked MIXED BALANCE, because that is what it is. With one precise limit: only the credit of the selected payee is offered. When searching by unit, the row gathers the shares of every co-owner, and on a unit with two owners it could happen that one person's credit paid the other's debt without the screen saying so. A co-owner's credit is still usable — you just have to select them as the payee.

Fixed — THE MESSAGE AFTER ISSUING NEVER REACHED ITS DESTINATION: the credit suggestion was written into the page banner, which appears for an instant and is immediately replaced by the «Issuing complete» dialog. It now travels on its own and lands inside that dialog, which stays until closed. That suggestion also flagged credits that cover nothing, sending the administrator to a page with nothing to do: it now names only the spendable ones, and with a single owner it also says which instalment is covered.

Under the hood: the offsettable amount is not a number but a pair of lists — which instalments the credit is drawn from, which instalments it covers — because the engine draws credit one instalment at a time and checks capacity on that instalment, so a per-person total is not enough to build a save that succeeds. The sentence describing the coverage lives in one place only, in the credit service: three surfaces display it, and the same sentence written in three places diverges at the first change. The debts of every owner in credit are read in a single query, because the widget sits on a page that opens on every access. The link generated by the administrator does not declare a request from the owner: they are two different things and the product kept them together, which is why the notice behaved backwards. Twenty new tests, seven of them on the frontend, including the first two on the payment screen, which had none.
